answer: A place that holds deep importance for my family is our ancestral home in the village, not far from Sirajganj, which has been in the family for generations. It is surrounded by rice fields, with a pond at the back and a big courtyard in the middle. Although we now live in a flat in town, this house remains a powerful symbol of our roots. My grandparents still live there, and my mother often goes to help look after them, so we are back and forth all the time. Every major family occasion, from weddings to Eid, seems to bring us all back there, and my elder sister travels from Dhaka with her children for the big celebrations. The house itself is old and simple, with a tin roof and wooden beams, but it is filled with [[sentimental]] value that no amount of money could replace. My father grew up there, and his old wooden school desk is still in one of the rooms. Walking through those rooms fills me with a strong sense of [[continuity]] and belonging. What makes it so important is that it connects the whole extended family across the generations, and my grandfather loves telling stories about the people who lived there before him. In a fast-changing world, having such an [[enduring]] anchor feels genuinely precious. Honestly, I hope we manage to keep it in the family for many years to come, even though some relatives have talked about selling part of the land. It is far more than a building; it is the [[cornerstone]] of our family's identity, and I feel [[deeply attached]] to it.

followUps.q: Do you think your family will keep the house?
followUps.answer: I really hope so. There is some talk about the land, but my father feels strongly that the house should stay in the family, and I think most of us agree with him.

followUps.q: Do young people in Bangladesh still care about their ancestral homes?
followUps.answer: Many do, especially at Eid, when huge numbers of people travel back to their villages. But as more young people settle in cities or abroad, those ties are becoming weaker, which I find a little sad.
